source_vibes_raw: Generate the MVM first and use it as the approved foundation for the ECM. Keep title_order, title_search, title_examination, title_finding, title_requirement, policy_exception, title_commitment, and title_policy as distinct entities. Keep settlement_statement and escrow_ledger as distinct entities. Model property, parcel, and legal_description separately. Model ownership as effective-dated ownership_interest records supported by evidence rather than a single current-owner attribute. Model party roles contextually so one party can hold multiple simultaneous roles. Preserve material lifecycle transitions, revisions, and prior classifications. Separate document execution_date, effective_date, submission_date, acceptance_date, and recording_date. Require evidence and provenance relationships for material title findings and underwriting decisions. Keep owner and lender policies as separate policy records and policy types. Every title policy must reference an originating title order. Treat bank account, wire instruction, identity document, signature, tax identifier, and non-public personal information as restricted. The MVM must cover core direct title and settlement workflows plus the minimum agency and claims concepts needed for end-to-end analysis. Expand detailed agency authority, audit, remittance, advanced claim financials, commercial transactions, regulatory reporting, fraud controls, retention, and legal hold primarily in the ECM. Use the synthetic Google Drive knowledge source IDs in documentation and requirement traceability where possible. Build metrics and semantic outputs around uniquely title-insurance questions: title clearance cycle time; open and aging title requirements; unresolved defects and liens; chain-of-title breaks; evidence completeness and provenance; curative action aging and effectiveness; underwriting referral and exception rates; commitment revision frequency; closing readiness; escrow receipt-disbursement reconciliation; recording rejection and resubmission rates; policy issuance lag after recording; owner-versus-lender policy coverage; agency remittance timeliness; claim frequency, severity, reserve, recovery, and loss ratio by title-risk cause. Keep search, examination, finding, requirement, exception, commitment, policy, settlement statement, escrow ledger, recording submission, and recorded instrument legally and operationally distinct. Genie-ready competency questions and metric definitions must use these title-specific concepts rather than generic insurance measures. Do not deploy physical schemas, tables, metric views, Genie agents, governed tags, domains, subdomains, or pages during this Dry Run. HARD SIZING DIRECTIVE: Generate exactly 7 domains and no more than 70 total products. Target 50 to 70 total products, with 7 to 10 products per domain. The seven required domains are operations, property, underwriting, settlement, recording, agency, and claim. Do not create additional domains. Place party, title evidence, search, examination, findings, requirements, curative actions, commitments, policies, endorsements, escrow, premiums, and remittances as products in the closest required domain while keeping the legally distinct entities separate. This sizing directive is a hard ceiling and overrides complexity-tier defaults.

Description of the specific use or activity permitted under the easement, e.g., installation and maintenance of underground utilities, pedestrian access, drainage.

Description of uses or activities expressly prohibited by the restriction or covenant, e.g., no structures within easement area, no commercial use, no subdivision below minimum lot size.

Five-digit FIPS county code identifying the county jurisdiction where the property is located. Used for county recorder routing, tax assessment, and regulatory reporting.
Complete verbatim text of the legal description as it appears in the recorded instrument or title commitment Schedule A. Authoritative SSOT for the legal description string.
Examiner or underwriter notes describing the nature of any identified gap between this legal description and the prior recorded description. Supports curative processing.
Flags whether a gap exists between the legal description in the current instrument and the prior recorded description, indicating potential chain-of-title break or gap coverage need.
Indicates whether this is the currently operative legal description for the associated parcel. True for the active version; False for superseded or historical versions.
Indicates whether this legal description has been reviewed and approved by the examiner or underwriter for use in the title commitment or policy Schedule A.
Unique surrogate identifier for the legal description record. Primary key for the legal_description entity in the property domain.
Lot number within the recorded subdivision or plat. Applicable when description_type is plat_subdivision or lot_block. Core identifier for platted parcels.
Narrative description of the point of beginning (POB) for a metes-and-bounds legal description. Applicable when description_type is metes_and_bounds.
Book number or volume of the recorded plat map in the county recorder's index. Used to locate the source plat document for title examination.

Aliquot part subdivisions within the PLSS section (e.g., NE1/4 of SW1/4). Applicable when description_type is plss. Provides precise parcel location within a section.
Name or code of the PLSS principal meridian governing the township/range/section coordinates (e.g., Willamette, Boise, 6th PM). Applicable when description_type is plss.
Range designation in the PLSS coordinate system (e.g., R3E, R7W). Applicable when description_type is plss. Used in chain-of-title and search indexing.
Section number (1–36) within the PLSS township/range grid. Applicable when description_type is plss. Core identifier for PLSS-based legal descriptions.
Two-letter US state code for the PLSS meridian context. Applicable only when description_type is plss. Identifies the principal meridian jurisdiction.
Township designation in the PLSS coordinate system (e.g., T2N, T5S). Applicable when description_type is plss. Used in chain-of-title and search indexing.
Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding version of this legal description. Enables chain-of-description history and prior classification preservation per VREQ-007.
Reference to the parent property entity. Enables direct linkage from legal description to the property record for title and underwriting workflows.

Official recording reference (book/page, document number, or instrument number) of the source instrument from which this legal description derives. Links description to county recorder index.
The legal description text as formatted and printed in the title commitment or policy Schedule A. May differ slightly from the raw recorded instrument text due to standardization.
Reference to the recorded instrument (deed, plat, or other document) from which this legal description was extracted. Supports evidence and provenance capture.
Normalized or standardized version of the legal description text produced by the title plant or search automation system for indexing and comparison purposes.
Two-letter US state abbreviation for the jurisdiction where the property is located. Used for state-specific title insurance rate filing and regulatory compliance.

Name of the licensed land surveyor or surveying firm that prepared the survey underlying this legal description. Used for evidence provenance and E&O tracking.

Unique surrogate identifier for each property lifecycle event record in the Property Information and County Data System.
The property type, vesting form, parcel status, or legal description classification established by this lifecycle event. Paired with prior_classification to document the transition.

Method by which the instrument was notarized: traditional in-person, Remote Online Notarization (RON), or In-Person Electronic Notarization (IPEN). Supports compliance and validity tracking.
Name of the notary public who acknowledged the instrument associated with this lifecycle event. Supports document validity verification and RON/IPEN compliance tracking.
Reference to the ownership_interest record created or superseded by this lifecycle event. Supports effective-dated ownership chain per VREQ-005.
Official page number within the deed book assigned by the county recorder. Used with book_number for traditional county recording cross-reference.
Reference to the parcel entity affected by this lifecycle event. Populated when the event is parcel-specific (e.g., parcel split/merge, APN reassignment).
The APN that existed before a parcel split, merge, or reassignment event. Null for non-parcel-change events. Supports parcel lineage and chain-of-title continuity.

The vesting language or tenancy form (e.g., joint tenancy, tenancy in common, community property) in effect before a vesting_change event. Null for non-vesting event types.
Reference to the property entity that is the subject of this lifecycle event. Establishes the authoritative property context for the event.
Name of the party (individual, title company, or attorney) who submitted the instrument for recording with the county recorder. Supports recording accountability and audit.
Date the instrument evidencing this lifecycle event was recorded with the county recorder or register of deeds. Per VREQ-008, distinct from execution_date and effective_date.

Foreign key linking to recording.recording_submission. Business justification: Lifecycle events track recording submission outcomes (acceptance, rejection, gap periods)—operational workflow for monitoring recording status, gap coverage periods, and policy
Sequential revision counter for this lifecycle event record. Starts at 1 for the original event; increments with each amendment. Supports lifecycle history tracking per VREQ-007.

Date the instrument was submitted to the county recorder for recording. Per VREQ-008, distinct from acceptance_date and recording_date. Supports recording rejection and resubmission tracking.
Self-referencing identifier of the prior lifecycle event that this record supersedes or amends. Null for original events. Preserves revision history and prior classifications per VREQ-007.
Foreign key linking to property.tax_assessment. Business justification: Tax assessment changes (supplemental assessments, appeals, tax lien filings) are material lifecycle events.

Reference to the title order in the Title Production System (e.g., SoftPro/RamQuest) that triggered or is associated with this lifecycle event. Supports end-to-end title workflow traceability.
Documentary transfer tax or deed stamp tax assessed on this lifecycle event by the county or state. Relevant for deed-type events; null for non-transfer events.
Timestamp when this lifecycle event record was last modified in the lakehouse Silver layer. Supports change data capture, audit trails, and incremental processing.
Nature of the transaction by which this ownership interest was acquired (e.g., purchase, gift, inheritance, foreclosure). Informs underwriting risk classification and chain-of-title analysis.
Deed book or volume number assigned by the county recorder where the instrument is indexed. Used in conjunction with page_number for traditional county plant lookups.

Reference to the recorded instrument or document that evidences this ownership interest (e.g., warranty deed, quit claim deed). Supports VREQ-005 evidence-backed ownership.
Free-text notes entered by the title examiner regarding this ownership interest record, including observations about vesting, authority, or chain-of-title issues.
Date the conveying instrument (deed) was signed by the grantor. Distinct from effective and recording dates per VREQ-008.

Classification of the estate or interest held (e.g., fee simple, life estate, leasehold). Determines the nature and scope of the ownership right conveyed.

Page number within the deed book where the instrument is recorded. Used with book_number for traditional county plant and title plant index lookups.
Reference to the parcel entity that this ownership interest encumbers. Links the interest to the authoritative parcel record in the property domain.

Previous interest_type or vesting_type classification before a reclassification event. Preserves lifecycle history of ownership classification changes per VREQ-007.
Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding ownership interest record in the chain of title. Enables linked-list traversal of the full ownership history.
Reference to the parent property entity. Provides the top-level real-property context for this ownership interest record.
Reason for any change in the ownership interest classification or status (e.g., correction of vesting language, court order, curative deed). Supports lifecycle history per VREQ-007.
Date the conveying instrument was officially recorded with the county recorder or register of deeds. Establishes constructive notice and priority. Distinct field per VREQ-008.
Identifier assigned by the source system of record to this ownership interest or conveying instrument. Enables traceability and reconciliation back to the originating system.
Code identifying the operational system of record from which this ownership interest record was sourced (e.g., title plant, county recorder, title production system).
Two-letter US state code where a corporate or LLC entity holding title was formed. Required for entity authority and good-standing verification in underwriting.
Documentary transfer tax or deed stamp tax assessed on the conveyance in USD. Calculated from consideration amount and applicable state/county tax rate.

Code identifying the operational system of record from which this property record was originally sourced (e.g., title production system, title plant, county data system). Supports data lineage and provenance tracking.

Code identifying the operational system of record from which this property record was originally sourced (e.g., title production system, title plant, county data system). Supports data lineage and provenance tracking.

Two-letter USPS state abbreviation for the state in which the property is located. Governs applicable state insurance regulations, recording statutes, and title plant jurisdiction.

Name of the recorded plat subdivision or development in which the property is located. Used in legal description assembly, title plant indexing, and CC&R identification.

Identifier of this evidence record in the originating source system (e.g., DataTrace document ID, Simplifile submission ID, county plant index key). Enables provenance traceability.

lineage.vibe: Model ownership as effective-dated ownership_interest records supported by evidence rather than a single current-owner attribute.
lineage.interpretation: Represent ownership via effective-dated ownership_interest records with evidence support, not a single current-owner field.

lineage.vibe: Model party roles contextually so that one party can hold multiple simultaneous roles.
lineage.interpretation: Support contextual party roles allowing a single party to hold multiple concurrent roles.

lineage.vibe: Preserve material lifecycle transitions, revisions, and prior classifications in the model.
lineage.interpretation: Retain lifecycle transitions, revisions, and prior classifications for material entities.

lineage.vibe: Separate document date attributes: execution_date, effective_date, submission_date, acceptance_date, and recording_date must each be distinct fields.
lineage.interpretation: Model document execution_date, effective_date, submission_date, acceptance_date, and recording_date as separate attributes.

lineage.vibe: Require evidence and provenance relationships for material title findings and underwriting decisions.
lineage.interpretation: Enforce evidence and provenance relationships supporting material title findings and underwriting decisions.

lineage.vibe: Keep owner and lender policies as separate policy records and separate policy types.
lineage.interpretation: Model owner policies and lender policies as distinct records and distinct policy types.

lineage.vibe: Every title policy must reference an originating title order.
lineage.interpretation: Enforce a mandatory relationship from each title policy back to an originating title order.

lineage.vibe: Treat bank account, wire instruction, identity document, signature, tax identifier, and non-public personal information (NPPI) as restricted/sensitive data.
lineage.interpretation: Classify bank account, wire instruction, identity document, signature, tax identifier, and NPPI as restricted data.

lineage.vibe: The MVM must cover core direct title and settlement workflows plus the minimum agency and claims concepts needed for end-to-end analysis.
lineage.interpretation: Scope the MVM to core direct title/settlement workflows plus minimal agency and claims concepts for end-to-end analysis.

lineage.vibe: Expand detailed agency authority, audit, remittance, advanced claim financials, commercial transactions, regulatory reporting, fraud controls, retention, and legal hold primarily in the ECM.
lineage.interpretation: Defer expanded coverage of agency authority, audit, remittance, advanced claim financials, commercial transactions, regulatory reporting, fraud controls, retention, and legal hold to the ECM.

lineage.vibe: Use the synthetic Google Drive knowledge source IDs in documentation and requirement traceability where possible.
lineage.interpretation: Reference synthetic Google Drive knowledge source IDs in documentation and requirement traceability.

lineage.vibe: Build metrics and semantic outputs around uniquely title-insurance questions: title clearance cycle time; open and aging title requirements; unresolved defects and liens; chain-of-title breaks; evidence completeness and provenance; curative action aging and effectiveness; underwriting referral and exception rates; commitment revision frequency; closing readiness; escrow receipt-disbursement reconciliation; recording rejection and resubmission rates; policy issuance lag after recording; owner-versus-lender policy coverage; agency remittance timeliness; and claim frequency, severity, reserve, recovery, and loss ratio by title-risk cause.
lineage.interpretation: Define metrics/semantic outputs around the enumerated title-insurance-specific measures.

lineage.vibe: Keep search, examination, finding, requirement, exception, commitment, policy, settlement statement, escrow ledger, recording submission, and recorded instrument legally and operationally distinct from one another.
lineage.interpretation: Maintain legal and operational distinction among these title/settlement/recording entities.

lineage.vibe: Genie-ready competency questions and metric definitions must use these title-specific concepts rather than generic insurance measures.
lineage.interpretation: Ensure competency questions and metric definitions use title-specific concepts, not generic insurance measures.

lineage.vibe: Do not deploy physical schemas, tables, metric views, Genie agents, governed tags, domains, subdomains, or pages during this Dry Run.
lineage.interpretation: Prohibit physical deployment of any artifacts during the Dry Run.

lineage.vibe: HARD SIZING DIRECTIVE: Generate exactly 7 domains and no more than 70 total products; target 50 to 70 total products, with 7 to 10 products per domain. This sizing directive is a hard ceiling and overrides complexity-tier defaults.
lineage.interpretation: Constrain the model to exactly 7 domains and 50-70 total products (7-10 per domain) as a hard ceiling.

lineage.vibe: The seven required domains are operations, property, underwriting, settlement, recording, agency, and claim. Do not create additional domains.
lineage.interpretation: Create exactly these seven named domains and no others.

Underwriting risk classification assigned to this GAP period based on duration, jurisdiction, instrument type, and rejection history. Drives escalation and monitoring workflows.
The date on which the GAP coverage window opens. Typically the closing date or the date of the last title search, whichever is later, per ALTA gap coverage standards.
Current lifecycle status of the GAP coverage window. Open indicates recording not yet confirmed; closed indicates recording confirmed; expired indicates coverage lapsed without recording.
Classification of the GAP coverage period by transaction type. Distinguishes standard purchase GAP from construction, HELOC, or refinance GAP windows with different risk profiles.
The unique instrument or document number assigned by the county recorder upon recording. Used as the primary recording reference in jurisdictions that do not use book/page.
Type of the primary instrument pending recording that is covered during the GAP period. Examples include Warranty Deed (WD), Deed of Trust (DOT), or mortgage.
Indicates whether the GAP coverage window has exceeded the maximum allowed duration. True triggers underwriting escalation and potential coverage review per policy guidelines.
Five-digit FIPS code identifying the county or jurisdiction where recording is required. Drives jurisdiction-specific GAP duration rules and recording turnaround benchmarks.
The most recent reason provided by the county recorder for rejecting the recording submission. Supports root-cause analysis of recording delays that extend the GAP window.
The date through which the title search was last run prior to closing. Used to establish the beginning of the GAP period when it precedes the closing date.
The maximum number of calendar days the GAP coverage window is permitted to remain open per underwriting guidelines or state regulatory requirements before escalation is required.
The official page number assigned by the county recorder upon acceptance of the recorded instrument. Combined with book_number forms the complete recording reference.
Number of calendar days between the confirmed recording_date and the date the title policy was issued. Directly supports the policy-issuance-lag-after-recording metric per VREQ-016.
The date on which the title policy was issued following confirmed recording. Used to compute policy_issuance_lag_days and to confirm the GAP window is fully resolved.
Indicates whether the GAP coverage applies to the Owner Title Policy (OTP), Lender Title Policy (LTP), or both. Drives separate owner-versus-lender coverage tracking per VREQ-010.
Monotonically incrementing version number for this GAP coverage period record. Supports optimistic concurrency control and revision history tracking per VREQ-007.
Precise timestamp when recording confirmation was received from the eRecording gateway or county recorder, marking the official close of the GAP coverage window.
The date on which the insured instruments were officially recorded by the county recorder or register of deeds, closing the GAP coverage window. Null until recording is confirmed.
Reference to the recording submission that, upon acceptance, closes the GAP coverage window. Links to the eRecording gateway submission record.
Number of times the recording submission was rejected by the county recorder prior to acceptance. Feeds the recording rejection and resubmission rate metric per VREQ-016.
The date of the most recent resubmission of instruments to the county recorder following a rejection. Null if no rejection has occurred.
Identifies the operational system of record from which this GAP coverage period record originated. Supports data lineage and provenance tracking across the title lifecycle.
Two-letter US state abbreviation for the jurisdiction where the property is located and recording is performed. Used for state-level regulatory and underwriting rule application.
The date on which the insured instruments were submitted to the county recorder or eRecording gateway. Distinct from closing_date, recording_date, and gap_start_date per VREQ-008.

Foreign key linking to claim.title_claim. Business justification: Gap coverage periods generate claims when intervening liens or defects arise during the gap. Claims adjuster must reference the gap period to validate coverage and determine liability.
Reference to the title commitment under which GAP coverage is extended. Identifies the commitment version in effect at closing.
Reference to the title order for which this GAP coverage period is being tracked. Links the GAP window to the originating order intake record.
Reference to the title policy (owner or lender) that incorporates or is affected by this GAP coverage period. Populated after policy issuance.
Classification of the underlying real estate transaction. Distinguishes purchase, refinance (REFI), HELOC, construction, and commercial transactions for GAP risk segmentation.
Timestamp when this GAP coverage period record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and lifecycle history preservation per VREQ-007.
Reference to the underwriting referral record created when the GAP window exceeded allowed thresholds or required non-standard resolution. Null if no referral was required.

Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding gateway transaction for the same recording_submission. Enables chain-of-resubmission traceability and lifecycle history preservation.

Indicates whether the confirmed recording reference number and recording_date have been fed back to the title policy and title lifecycle records. Supports evidence completeness and provenance tracking.
Date and time the recording reference number and recording_date were successfully fed back to the title production system and policy records. Null until provenance_fed_back is true.

Official date the document was recorded by the county recorder, as stamped on the recorded instrument. Distinct from submission_timestamp. Drives GAP coverage window closure and policy issuance lag metrics.
Total recording fee amount submitted to the county recorder with this gateway transaction, in US dollars. Includes per-page and per-document fees as applicable by jurisdiction.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the recording fee amount. Typically USD for domestic US title transactions.
Official recording reference number assigned by the county recorder upon acceptance, including book and page or instrument number. Null until county acceptance is confirmed.
Reference to the parent recording_submission that initiated this gateway transaction. Links the gateway exchange back to the title lifecycle recording event.
Precise date and time the document was officially recorded by the county recorder, including time-of-day where available. Supports GAP period calculation at minute-level precision.

Service level agreement target turnaround time in hours from submission to county acceptance for this transaction, based on jurisdiction and transaction type.
Two-letter USPS state abbreviation for the jurisdiction where the document is being recorded. Used for state-level regulatory reporting and recording fee schedules.
Date and time the document package was transmitted outbound to the eRecording gateway. Principal business event timestamp for this transaction. Used to measure recording cycle time.
Name of the title company, branch, or independent agent organization that submitted the gateway transaction. Relevant for agency channel recording oversight.

Indicates whether this jurisdiction accepts documents notarized via In-Person Electronic Notarization (IPEN). Used alongside ron_accepted to determine eligible closing modalities.
Unique surrogate identifier for each county recorder or register of deeds jurisdiction record in the title insurance recording master reference.
Timestamp when this jurisdiction record was most recently modified. Used to detect stale fee schedules, outdated submission channel flags, or changed office contact information.

Date on which the jurisdiction record details (fees, channels, contact info) were last verified against the official county recorder source. Supports data quality monitoring and stale-reference alerting.
Indicates whether this jurisdiction accepts document submissions via postal mail. Used as a fallback channel when eRecording is unavailable or rejected.
Minimum margin size in inches required on all pages of documents submitted to this jurisdiction. Non-compliant margins are a common rejection cause; used in document preparation validation.
Number of pages included in the base recording fee before per-page charges apply. Used with fee_per_page_amount to compute total recording fees for documents exceeding the base page threshold.
Indicates whether notarization is required for documents submitted to this jurisdiction. Drives closing workflow requirements for notary scheduling and RON/IPEN eligibility.
Primary street address line of the recording office, used for mail and in-person document submission. Required when eRecording is unavailable or rejected documents must be physically resubmitted.
Secondary address line (suite, floor, room number) for the recording office. Supplements office_address_line1 for precise physical delivery of documents.
City in which the recording office is physically located. Used in conjunction with state_code and office_zip_code for mail submission addressing and courier routing.
Official email address for the recording office, used for submission inquiries, rejection notices, and correspondence regarding recorded instruments.
Fax number for the recording office, used in jurisdictions that accept fax-based document submission or rejection notice delivery.
Standard business hours of the recording office (e.g., 'Mon-Fri 08:00-17:00 CT'). Used to determine same-day recording eligibility and courier delivery scheduling.
Primary telephone number for the recording office, used to resolve rejection inquiries, confirm receipt of mailed documents, and coordinate resubmission.
Current operational status of the recording jurisdiction. Inactive or merged jurisdictions are retained for historical recording reference but blocked from new submission routing.
Public website URL for the recording office, providing access to fee schedules, accepted document formats, cover-sheet requirements, and online search portals.
USPS ZIP or ZIP+4 code for the recording office mailing address. Used for mail submission routing and courier delivery confirmation.

Indicates whether a title plant (DataTrace, TitlePoint, or county plant index) provides automated search coverage for this jurisdiction. Drives search channel selection in the title production system.
Name of the title plant or automated search provider covering this jurisdiction (e.g., DataTrace, TitlePoint). Used for search order routing and vendor management.

Type of recording act governing priority of recorded instruments in this jurisdiction: race (first to record wins), notice (subsequent BFP without notice wins), or race_notice (both conditions required). Critical for chain-of-title analysis.
Official name of the county recorder, register of deeds, or equivalent recording authority (e.g., 'Travis County Clerk', 'Cook County Recorder of Deeds'). Used on cover sheets and submission routing.

Classification of the recording authority type, which varies by state (e.g., county_recorder in CA, register_of_deeds in MI, county_clerk in TX). Drives cover-sheet template and fee schedule selection.

Format used by this jurisdiction to assign recording references to accepted instruments (e.g., book/page, instrument number, document number). Determines how recording_reference_number is parsed and stored.
Observed percentage of document submissions rejected by this jurisdiction, based on historical submission data. Used for recording rejection/resubmission rate metrics and operational risk monitoring.
Indicates whether this jurisdiction accepts documents notarized via Remote Online Notarization (RON). Drives closing channel eligibility and notarization workflow routing.
Local time (HH:MM, 24-hour) by which a document must be submitted to qualify for same-day recording in this jurisdiction. Critical for gap-period management and closing scheduling.
Two-letter USPS state abbreviation for the state in which this recording jurisdiction is located (e.g., TX, CA, FL). Used for state-level recording rule application and regulatory routing.

Free-text field capturing jurisdiction-specific recording requirements, exceptions, or procedural notes not captured in structured fields (e.g., special deed tax stamps, unique cover sheet rules, holiday closures).
IANA time zone identifier for the recording office (e.g., 'America/Chicago'). Used to calculate same-day recording cutoff times and gap-period timestamps accurately.

Specifies the taxable basis for documentary transfer tax in this jurisdiction (e.g., full consideration, equity only, loan amount). Required for accurate transfer tax calculation on the settlement statement.

Documentary transfer tax rate applied to the consideration amount for deed recordings in this jurisdiction, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.001100 for $1.10 per $1,000). Used for settlement fee calculation.

Indicates whether title was determined insurable (though not necessarily marketable) at policy issuance. Distinct from marketable_title_flag for underwriting risk classification.
Full legal name of the insured party as it appears on Schedule A of the policy. For OTP this is the buyer/owner; for LTP this is the lender/mortgagee.
Classification of the insured party: individual person, legal entity (LLC/Corp), trust, estate, or government body. Drives vesting and coverage analysis.
Date the title policy was formally issued by the underwriter or issuing agent. Principal business event date for policy issuance lag metrics.
Name of the lender/mortgagee insured under an LTP policy as shown on Schedule A. Null for OTP policies.
Maximum dollar amount of coverage (face amount) for which the underwriter is liable under this policy. For OTP equals purchase price; for LTP equals loan amount.
Principal loan amount secured by the insured mortgage, applicable to LTP policies only. Equals the LTP liability amount and is used for LTV and coverage analysis.
Lender-assigned loan number for the mortgage insured under an LTP policy. Used to cross-reference with lender systems and MERS registration.
Indicates whether the underwriter determined title to be marketable at the time of policy issuance. Supports insurable vs. marketable title determination tracking.
Premium amount after applying reissue credits and other adjustments. Represents the actual premium collected and subject to remittance split.
Number of Schedule B-II exceptions (policy_exception records) carried on this policy at issuance. Supports unresolved defect and exception rate metrics per VREQ-016.
ALTA or state-specific policy form identifier (e.g., ALTA 2021 Owner's Policy, ALTA 2021 Loan Policy, ALTA Homeowner's Policy 2013). Governs coverage terms.
Number of calendar days between the recording_date of the insured instrument and the policy issue_date. Key metric for policy issuance lag after recording per VREQ-016.
Externally-known unique policy number assigned by the underwriter or title production system (e.g., SoftPro/RamQuest). Used for claims, endorsements, and regulatory reporting.
Current lifecycle state of the title policy. Tracks progression from draft through issuance, and captures cancellations or reissuances for revision history per VREQ-007.
Discriminates between Owner's Title Policy (OTP) and Lender's/Loan Title Policy (LTP). Owner and lender policies are stored as separate records with separate policy_type values per VREQ-010.
Gross title insurance premium charged for this policy before any splits or adjustments. Used for premium revenue recognition and remittance calculations.
Issue date of the prior title policy referenced for reissue credit calculation. Required by state rate filings to validate reissue credit eligibility.
Policy number of a previously issued title policy on the same property, used to establish reissue credit eligibility and chain-of-coverage continuity.
Channel through which the policy was produced: direct branch, centralized lender channel, or independent title agent. Drives remittance, oversight, and performance metrics.

Foreign key linking to property.property. Business justification: Every title policy insures a specific property. Direct link is fundamental for policy-to-property traceability, claim analysis by property characteristics, loss ratio calculation by
Date the insured instrument (deed or mortgage) was recorded at the county recorder/register of deeds. Anchors the gap period and effective date. Distinct per VREQ-008.
Dollar credit applied to the premium when a prior policy exists on the same property and a reissue rate is applicable. Reduces net premium charged.
Indicates whether this policy was issued at a reissue rate based on a prior policy. Triggers reissue credit calculation and prior policy validation.
Actual date the underwriter's premium share was remitted by the agent. Null if not yet remitted. Used to calculate remittance lag.
Date by which the agent must remit the underwriter's share of the premium per the agency agreement. Used for remittance timeliness tracking.
Current status of the underwriter premium remittance for this policy. Supports agency remittance timeliness metrics per VREQ-016.
Indicates whether this policy was issued simultaneously with a companion OTP or LTP policy on the same transaction, qualifying for a simultaneous issue rate discount.
Native policy identifier from the originating title production system (e.g., SoftPro Select, RamQuest Horizon, Qualia). Enables traceability back to the system of record.
Two-letter US state code where the insured property is located. Governs applicable rate filings, policy forms, and regulatory reporting jurisdiction.
Reference to the title commitment (Schedule A/B-I/B-II) from which this policy was issued. Links policy to the approved commitment that preceded it.
Reference to the originating title order that initiated the search, examination, commitment, and policy production workflow. Every title_policy must trace to a title_order.
Unique surrogate identifier for the title insurance policy record. Primary key for the title_policy entity.
Type of real estate transaction underlying the policy (purchase, refinance, HELOC, construction, home equity, commercial). Drives rate, form, and coverage selection.
Code identifying the title underwriter (e.g., FNF, FAF, STC, ORI) that backs this policy. Required for regulatory reporting and loss ratio analysis.
Dollar portion of the net premium remitted to the underwriter per the agency agreement split schedule. Drives remittance timeliness metrics.
Indicates whether this policy required an underwriting referral (UWR) to the underwriter's home office or senior underwriter prior to issuance. Drives UWR rate metrics.
Timestamp when this title_policy record was last modified in the system of record. Supports change detection and lifecycle history per VREQ-007.
Start date when this record version became effective
End date when this record version ceased to be effective (NULL if current)
Date this requirement was formally added to the title commitment as a Schedule B-I item. May differ from identified_date if added during a commitment revision.
Indicates whether this requirement applies to the owner policy (OTP), lender policy (LTP), or both. Supports owner-versus-lender coverage analysis per VREQ-010.
Name or identifier of the internal curative processor or title officer assigned to manage resolution of this requirement. Supports workload and aging analysis.
Date and time when this record was last modified
User or process that last modified this record
Identifies the commitment schedule section where this item appears. Title requirements appear in Schedule B-I (requirements to be satisfied before policy issuance).
Confirmed dollar amount from the payoff demand letter or lien release documentation. Supersedes estimated_payoff_amount once verified. Used for final settlement reconciliation.
User or process that created this record
Timestamp when this title requirement record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and curative aging baseline calculations.
Date and time when this record was created

Specific curative action being taken to resolve this requirement (e.g., obtain payoff, order release, record document). Aligns with CPM/GAPcure workflow steps. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product]
Reference number or identifier of the Curative Processing Memo (CPM) associated with the resolution effort for this requirement. Links to document management system.
Target date by which this requirement must be satisfied to support the scheduled closing date. Used for curative aging and closing readiness dashboards.
Estimated dollar amount required to satisfy this requirement (e.g., mortgage payoff, tax lien amount, judgment amount). Used for settlement statement preparation and escrow funding.
Document management system reference (document ID or URL) for the evidence supporting satisfaction of this requirement (e.g., recorded release, payoff confirmation letter).
Indicates whether gap coverage is required for this requirement, meaning the curative action must address the gap period between search date and recording date (GAPcure).
Name of the grantee on the instrument underlying this requirement. Used for chain-of-title verification and vesting confirmation.
Name of the grantor on the instrument underlying this requirement (e.g., lender to be paid off, judgment creditor). Used for lien identification and payoff demand.
Calendar date on which this requirement was first identified during title examination. Start point for curative aging calculations and SLA tracking.
Recording reference (book/page, document number, or instrument number) of the recorded instrument underlying this requirement. Supports chain-of-title tracing.
Indicates whether this record is the current active version of the requirement. False for superseded versions retained for lifecycle history. Supports bi-temporal querying.
Indicates whether this requirement must be satisfied before closing can proceed. True = hard closing block; False = may be satisfied post-closing with escrow holdback.
Indicates whether this requirement was escalated to the underwriter for a formal underwriting referral (UWR) decision. Supports UW referral rate metrics.
Type of lien or encumbrance underlying this requirement when the requirement involves lien clearance (e.g., DOT, tax lien, mechanics lien, HOA). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product]
Free-text operational notes entered by the curative processor or examiner regarding the status, contacts, or special handling instructions for this requirement.
Reference to the title examination session during which this requirement was identified. Supports provenance tracing from examination to curative action.

Foreign key linking to property.parcel. Business justification: Requirements often apply to specific parcels (tax liens, easements, boundary issues). Parcel-level tracking enables curative action targeting, Schedule B exception mapping by parcel
Date through which the confirmed payoff amount is valid. Closing must occur on or before this date to honor the payoff figure. Critical for closing scheduling.
Self-referencing link to the previous version of this requirement record when a material revision occurred. Preserves lifecycle history per VREQ-007.
Operational priority assigned to this requirement for curative processing. Critical items block closing; high items require expedited action before commitment expiry.
County recorder book/page or instrument number for the document recorded to satisfy this requirement (e.g., recorded deed of reconveyance, release of lien). Supports chain-of-title.

Broad grouping of the requirement for reporting and aging analysis (e.g., lien clearance, vesting, survey, tax). Supports open/aging requirement metrics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product]
Full narrative text of the Schedule B-I requirement as it appears on the commitment. Describes the specific curative action required of the parties before policy issuance.
Human-readable Schedule B-I item number as it appears on the commitment (e.g., B-I-1, B-I-2). Used for external communication with parties and lenders.
Identifies who or what system originated this requirement (examiner, underwriter, lender instruction, automated search engine). Supports provenance and audit.
Current lifecycle state of the Schedule B-I requirement. Drives closing readiness and open/aging requirement dashboards. Transitions: open → in_progress → satisfied or waived.
Categorical classification of the curative action required (e.g., payoff, release, satisfaction, subordination). Drives workflow routing and curative processing.
Role of the party responsible for satisfying this requirement (e.g., seller must provide payoff, buyer must provide survey). Drives task assignment in curative workflow.

Sequential revision number tracking changes to this requirement across commitment revisions. Version 1 = original; increments with each material change. Supports commitment revision frequency metrics.
Date on which this requirement was confirmed as satisfied (e.g., payoff received, release recorded). Null if not yet satisfied. Used for curative effectiveness metrics.
Method by which this requirement was ultimately satisfied or resolved (e.g., payoff and release, recorded release, affidavit, court order, underwriter waiver, escrow holdback).
Native identifier of this requirement in the originating title production system (e.g., SoftPro Select, RamQuest Horizon, Qualia). Used for system-of-record reconciliation.
Reference to the title commitment on which this requirement appears as a Schedule B-I item. Null if requirement predates commitment issuance.
Reference to the specific title finding (defect, lien, encumbrance, or cloud on title) that necessitated this Schedule B-I requirement. Core provenance link.
Foreign key reference to the originating title order that generated this Schedule B-I requirement. Links the requirement to its parent transaction context.
Unique surrogate primary key for the title requirement record (Schedule B-I item). Globally unique across all requirement records in the title production system.
Foreign key linking to operations.title_search. Business justification: Requirements often cite specific search findings (instrument references, recording dates).
Timestamp of the most recent modification to this title requirement record. Used for change detection, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing.
Reference to the underwriting referral record if this requirement triggered a formal UWR. Null when is_underwriter_referral is False.
Name or identifier of the underwriter or authorized officer who approved the waiver of this requirement. Required when requirement_status is waived. Supports audit trail.
Date on which this requirement was formally waived by the underwriter or authorized officer. Null if not waived. Requires waiver_authority and waiver_reason to be populated.
Narrative explanation for why this requirement was waived rather than satisfied. Required for audit and regulatory compliance when a Schedule B-I item is removed without curative action.
Assessor's Parcel Number (APN) or Parcel Identification Number (PIN) assigned by the county assessor for the subject property. Key cross-reference to property and parcel records.
Indicates whether the examiner identified a break or gap in the chain of title (COT) during examination. Key metric for unresolved defect and lien reporting (VREQ-016).
Date and time when this record was last modified
User or process that last modified this record
User or process that created this record
Date and time when this examination record was first created in the system. Audit field supporting record provenance and SLA measurement from order intake.
Date and time when this record was created
Indicates whether one or more curative processing actions (CPM/GAPcure) are required to clear title defects identified in this examination before commitment issuance.

Classification of the primary curative action required (e.g., lien release, reconveyance, satisfaction, gap cure, quiet title). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: lien_release|reconveyance|satisfaction|gap_cure|quiet_title|subordination — promote to reference product]
Target date by which all curative actions must be completed to meet the scheduled closing date. Supports curative action aging and effectiveness metrics (VREQ-016).
Type of estate or interest in the property being insured as identified during examination: fee simple, leasehold, life estate, or easement. Populates Schedule A of the commitment.
Precise date and time the examiner finalized the examination and released findings. Used to compute title clearance cycle time and examiner throughput metrics.
Calendar date on which the title examiner completed the formal review of the assembled search results. Principal business event date for cycle-time measurement.
Externally visible alphanumeric identifier assigned to this examination by the title production system (e.g., SoftPro/RamQuest). Used for cross-system traceability.
Free-text notes describing the scope, limitations, or special conditions of the examination (e.g., limited search period, missing instruments, county plant gaps). Supports evidence provenance.
Precise date and time the examiner began reviewing the search package. Used with completion timestamp to compute title clearance cycle time (VREQ-016).

Current lifecycle state of the title examination record. Drives workflow routing and closing-readiness metrics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|in_review|completed|revised|cancelled — promote to reference product if states expand]
Classification of the scope of examination: full chain-of-title review, limited/O&E, update/bring-down, or gap-period examination. Drives examiner effort and risk assessment.
State-issued license or bar number of the title examiner or attorney who performed the examination. Required for regulatory compliance and examiner credential verification.
Formal written opinion or summary conclusion of the title examiner regarding the state of title, including any qualifications or conditions. Core evidence and provenance field (VREQ-007).
Reference to the party record for the licensed title examiner or attorney who performed the examination. Supports examiner identity and workload analytics.
Two-letter US state code where the examiner is licensed to perform title examinations. Ensures jurisdiction-appropriate examination standards are applied.
Number of Schedule B-II policy exceptions (policy_exception records) identified during examination. Supports owner-versus-lender coverage and exception rate metrics.
Total number of title_finding records generated from this examination. Supports open/aging defect metrics and examiner productivity reporting (VREQ-016).
Indicates whether gap coverage is required between the search-through date and the anticipated recording date. Triggers gap curative (GAPcure) workflow.
Indicates whether a judgment lien against the vested owner or property was identified during examination. Requires curative clearance before policy issuance.
Indicates whether a lien search (judgment liens, tax liens, mechanics liens, HOA assessments) was included in the examination scope. Affects unresolved lien metrics.
Indicates whether a lis pendens (LP) — notice of pending litigation — was identified against the subject property during examination. Significant underwriting risk factor.
Examiner's determination of title quality: marketable, insurable (with exceptions), uninsurable, or conditional pending curative action. Drives underwriting referral and commitment issuance.
Indicates whether a mechanics lien or materialman's lien was identified against the subject property during examination. Common in construction transactions.
Number of Schedule B-I title requirements (title_requirement records) that remain open/uncleared at the time of last update. Drives open and aging requirements metric (VREQ-016).
Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding examination record for this order. Preserves revision lineage and material lifecycle transitions (VREQ-007).
Effective date of the prior owner's title policy identified during examination. Used to determine prior policy rate eligibility and search period requirements.
Policy number of any prior owner's title policy (OTP) identified during examination. Used for prior policy rate eligibility and evidence of prior insured title.
Five-digit FIPS county code for the county in which the subject property is located. Used for county recorder routing, plant access, and jurisdiction-level reporting.
Two-letter US state code of the subject property being examined. Determines applicable state title law, recording requirements, and underwriting guidelines.

Sequential revision counter for this examination record. Increments when the examination is updated due to new search results, curative completions, or examiner corrections. Supports lifecycle history (VREQ-007).
Reason for revising a prior examination (e.g., updated search results, curative completion, examiner correction, new lien discovered). Supports commitment revision frequency metric (VREQ-016).
The earliest date from which the chain-of-title search was assembled. Together with search_through_date defines the full search period examined.
The effective date through which the title search was run and the examiner reviewed. Defines the gap period boundary for gap coverage (GAP) analysis.
Code identifying the title production system of record from which this examination record originated (e.g., SoftPro Select, RamQuest Horizon, Qualia). Supports data lineage.
Native identifier for this examination record in the originating title production system (SoftPro/RamQuest/Qualia). Enables cross-system reconciliation and audit traceability.
Indicates whether a federal or state tax lien was identified against the subject property or vested owner during examination. Triggers curative requirement.
Reference to the originating title order that triggered this examination. Every examination must trace back to a title order per ALTA workflow standards.
Reference to the title search record whose assembled chain-of-title results are being examined. Examination is legally distinct from search per VREQ-017.
Type of real-estate transaction driving the examination: purchase, refinance (REFI), home-equity line of credit (HELOC), construction, or commercial. Affects examination scope and underwriting risk.
Free-text or coded reason explaining why the examination was escalated for underwriting review (e.g., chain-of-title break, unresolved lien, high-risk vesting). Supports UWR rate analysis.
Indicates whether this examination requires escalation to an underwriter for risk review (UWR). Drives underwriting referral rate metric (VREQ-016).
Unique surrogate identifier for the title examination record. Primary key for the underwriting_title_examination entity in the Silver layer.
Date and time when this examination record was last modified. Audit field supporting change detection, incremental ETL, and lifecycle history tracking (VREQ-007).
Form of title vesting identified during examination (e.g., joint tenancy, tenancy in common, community property, sole ownership, trust). Drives Schedule A vesting language.
Identifier of the independent title agent, if the referral originates from an independent agency channel. Null for direct branch or centralized lender orders.
Date and time when this record was last modified
User or process that last modified this record
Business channel through which the originating title order was produced: direct branch, centralized lender, or independent agent. Supports channel-level UWR rate reporting.
Indicates whether this underwriting referral caused or is at risk of causing a delay to the scheduled closing date. Supports closing readiness metrics per VREQ-016.
Free-text description of conditions, requirements, or curative actions imposed by the underwriter as part of an approved-with-conditions decision. Maps to Schedule B-I requirements.
User or process that created this record
Timestamp when this underwriting referral record was first created in the lakehouse Silver layer. Audit trail for data lineage and provenance per VREQ-007.
Date and time when this record was created
Narrative description of the curative processing steps required to clear the title defect or satisfy underwriting conditions. Supports curative aging and effectiveness metrics.
Indicates whether the underwriting decision requires curative processing (CPM/GAPcure) before the commitment or policy can be issued. True = curative action required.
Date on which all required curative actions were confirmed as completed and accepted by the underwriter. Used to measure curative effectiveness and cycle time.
Target date by which curative actions must be completed to maintain the scheduled closing date. Drives curative aging and closing readiness metrics.
Detailed narrative of the title defect, cloud on title, lien, or encumbrance under underwriting review. Provides examiner context for the underwriter's risk assessment.
Indicates whether the underwriting decision requires one or more ALTA endorsements (e.g., ALTA 9, ALTA 8.1, ALTA 22) to be attached to the policy.
Comma-separated list of ALTA endorsement form numbers required as a result of this referral decision (e.g., ALTA 9, ALTA 8.1, ALTA 22). Populated when endorsement_required is True.
Number of times this referral has been escalated to a higher underwriting authority level. Supports complexity and exception rate analytics.
Indicates whether the underwriting decision resulted in a Schedule B-II policy exception being added to the commitment or policy. True = exception scheduled.
End date of the gap coverage period under review, typically the anticipated recording date. Defines the gap window for which underwriting approval is sought.
Start date of the gap coverage period under review, applicable when referral_type is gap_coverage. Represents the date through which the title search was completed.
Underwriter's determination of the title's insurability or marketability following review. Core output of the UWR process; drives policy issuance eligibility.
Total insured liability amount (policy face value) associated with the transaction at the time of referral. High-liability thresholds are a primary UWR trigger. USD.
Indicates whether the transaction liability amount exceeded the underwriter's authority threshold, triggering mandatory referral. True = threshold exceeded.
Reference to the policy_exception record created as a result of this underwriting referral decision. Populated when exception_scheduled is True.
Indicates whether the referral pertains to an owner title policy (OTP), lender title policy (LTP), or both. Supports owner-versus-lender coverage metrics per VREQ-010.
Reference number of a prior title insurance claim on the same property or related parties that contributed to this referral trigger. Links to claims administration history.
Self-referential link to the previous version of this referral when revision_number > 1. Preserves material lifecycle history and revision chain per VREQ-007.
Foreign key linking to property.property. Business justification: Referrals are triggered by property-specific risks (title defects, chain breaks, high liability).
Calendar date on which the underwriting referral was formally submitted for review. Principal business event date; used as the start point for UWR cycle time measurement.
Human-readable, externally referenceable identifier for this underwriting referral, formatted as UWR-YYYY-NNNNNN. Used in correspondence with underwriters and in audit trails.

Current lifecycle state of the underwriting referral. Drives open/aging UWR metrics and commitment readiness. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open|pending_uw_review|approved|approved_with_conditions|declined|withdrawn — promote to reference product]
Precise date-time when the underwriting referral was submitted. Provides intraday precision for SLA measurement and audit trail beyond the referral_date.
Free-text narrative describing the specific condition, defect, or risk factor that triggered escalation to underwriting review. Complements referral_type with examiner detail.
Classification of the primary reason for escalation to underwriting review. Supports UWR rate analytics by trigger category. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product]
Sequential revision counter for this underwriting referral, incremented when material changes are submitted for re-review. Supports commitment revision frequency metrics per VREQ-016.

Categorical classification of the title risk type under review. Aligns with title-risk cause taxonomy used in claim frequency and severity reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product]
Indicates whether the underwriting decision was rendered after the sla_target_days threshold. True = SLA breached. Supports aging and cycle time reporting.
Number of business days within which the underwriting decision is contractually or operationally required. Baseline for UWR cycle time SLA compliance measurement.
Identifier of this referral record in the originating Underwriting Risk and Policy Management System (e.g., SoftPro, RamQuest, or proprietary UW system). Supports SoR reconciliation.
Reference to the title commitment associated with this referral, if the referral arises at or after commitment stage. Nullable when referral precedes commitment issuance.
Reference to the specific title finding (defect, lien, encumbrance, or cloud on title) that is the primary subject of this underwriting referral.
Reference to the title order that triggered this underwriting referral. Every UWR must trace back to an originating title order.
Type of real estate transaction associated with the referral (e.g., purchase, REFI, HELOC, construction, commercial). Supports segmentation of UWR rates by transaction type.
Reference to the title examination that surfaced the defect or risk condition prompting this underwriting referral.
Timestamp when this underwriting referral record was last modified in the lakehouse Silver layer. Supports change detection and audit trail for lifecycle transitions.
Identifier of the underwriter assigned to review and decide on this referral. Supports underwriter workload, cycle time, and decision-rate analytics.
Level of underwriting authority required to approve this referral (branch, regional, national, or reinsurance). Reflects the risk complexity and liability amount thresholds.
Final underwriting decision rendered on this referral. Drives commitment issuance, exception scheduling, and curative action requirements.
Date on which the underwriter rendered a decision (approved, approved with conditions, or declined) on this referral. Used to compute UWR cycle time.
Narrative explanation provided by the underwriter supporting the decision. Required for declined and approved-with-conditions outcomes for audit and regulatory review.
Identifier of the title examiner or branch staff member who initiated the underwriting referral. Supports examiner-level UWR rate and workload analytics.
Unique surrogate identifier for the underwriting referral record. Primary key for the uw_referral entity.

lineage.vibe: Place party, title evidence, search, examination, findings, requirements, curative actions, commitments, policies, endorsements, escrow, premiums, and remittances as products in the closest required domain while keeping the legally distinct entities separate.
lineage.interpretation: Assign the enumerated products to the closest of the seven required domains while preserving legal distinctness.

missed.vibe: Keep title_order, title_search, title_examination, title_finding, title_requirement, policy_exception, title_commitment, and title_policy as distinct, separate entities.
missed.interpretation: Preserve each of these title workflow concepts as separate entities.

missed.vibe: Keep settlement_statement and escrow_ledger as distinct, separate entities.
missed.interpretation: Model settlement_statement and escrow_ledger as separate entities.

missed.vibe: Model property, parcel, and legal_description as three separate entities.
missed.interpretation: Separate property, parcel, and legal_description into distinct entities.

missed.vibe: Model ownership as effective-dated ownership_interest records supported by evidence rather than a single current-owner attribute.
missed.interpretation: Represent ownership via effective-dated ownership_interest records with evidence support, not a single current-owner field.

missed.vibe: Model party roles contextually so that one party can hold multiple simultaneous roles.
missed.interpretation: Support contextual party roles allowing a single party to hold multiple concurrent roles.

missed.vibe: Require evidence and provenance relationships for material title findings and underwriting decisions.
missed.interpretation: Enforce evidence and provenance relationships supporting material title findings and underwriting decisions.

missed.vibe: Keep owner and lender policies as separate policy records and separate policy types.
missed.interpretation: Model owner policies and lender policies as distinct records and distinct policy types.

missed.vibe: Every title policy must reference an originating title order.
missed.interpretation: Enforce a mandatory relationship from each title policy back to an originating title order.

missed.vibe: Treat bank account, wire instruction, identity document, signature, tax identifier, and non-public personal information (NPPI) as restricted/sensitive data.
missed.interpretation: Classify bank account, wire instruction, identity document, signature, tax identifier, and NPPI as restricted data.

missed.vibe: Build metrics and semantic outputs around uniquely title-insurance questions: title clearance cycle time; open and aging title requirements; unresolved defects and liens; chain-of-title breaks; evidence completeness and provenance; curative action aging and effectiveness; underwriting referral and exception rates; commitment revision frequency; closing readiness; escrow receipt-disbursement reconciliation; recording rejection and resubmission rates; policy issuance lag after recording; owner-versus-lender policy coverage; agency remittance timeliness; and claim frequency, severity, reserve, recovery, and loss ratio by title-risk cause.
missed.interpretation: Define metrics/semantic outputs around the enumerated title-insurance-specific measures.

missed.vibe: Keep search, examination, finding, requirement, exception, commitment, policy, settlement statement, escrow ledger, recording submission, and recorded instrument legally and operationally distinct from one another.
missed.interpretation: Maintain legal and operational distinction among these title/settlement/recording entities.

missed.vibe: Place party, title evidence, search, examination, findings, requirements, curative actions, commitments, policies, endorsements, escrow, premiums, and remittances as products in the closest required domain while keeping the legally distinct entities separate.
missed.interpretation: Assign the enumerated products to the closest of the seven required domains while preserving legal distinctness.
